experiments.name: Sticky add-to-cart bar on mobile product pages
experiments.hypothesis: On mobile, the add-to-cart button scrolls out of view while shoppers read reviews and the label. Keeping it pinned will raise add-to-cart rate without lowering order value.
experiments.audience: Android + iOS app sessions that view a product page

experiments.name: One-page checkout (address + payment on one screen)
experiments.hypothesis: Collapsing address and payment into one screen removes a step and lifts checkout completion.
experiments.audience: Web + Android sessions that start checkout

impact.title: iOS 4.2 broke UPI payments
impact.assumption: Recover the full difference-in-differences gap vs Android once the UPI intent bug is fixed.

impact.title: Heavy-item delivery fee surprises mass gainer carts
impact.assumption: Close half the cart → checkout gap to other carts by showing the fee on the product page (or absorbing it).

impact.title: Coupons fail at checkout
impact.assumption: Half the payment-rate gap closes when the minimum cart value is shown before the code is typed.

impact.title: One in seven searches finds nothing
impact.assumption: Synonyms and spell-correction bring half of zero-result sessions to the found-results conversion rate.

sql.weekly_kpis:
-- Weekly sessions, orders, revenue and conversion. The founder's question in one
-- table: is traffic growing faster than orders?
SELECT
  to_char(date_trunc('week', day), 'YYYY-MM-DD')                         AS week,
  count(*)::int                                                           AS sessions,
  count(DISTINCT user_id)::int                                            AS users,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased)::int                                  AS orders,
  round(sum(revenue))::float8                                             AS revenue,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased) / count(*), 2)::float8  AS cvr_pct,
  round(sum(revenue) / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased), 0))::float8 AS aov
FROM sessions
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
sql.funnel_overall:
-- Strict session funnel: each step only counts sessions that reached every earlier step.
SELECT step, sessions::int FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS ord, 'Session started' AS step, count(*) AS sessions FROM sessions
  UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'Viewed a product', count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed) FROM sessions
  UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'Added to cart',    count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed AND carted) FROM sessions
  UNION ALL SELECT 4, 'Started checkout', count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed AND carted AND checkout) FROM sessions
  UNION ALL SELECT 5, 'Paid',             count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed AND carted AND checkout AND purchased) FROM sessions
) f
ORDER BY ord;
sql.funnel_by_segment:
-- The same strict funnel cut four ways; "dimension" names the cut.
WITH s AS (
  SELECT *,
    viewed AND carted                            AS f_cart,
    viewed AND carted AND checkout               AS f_checkout,
    viewed AND carted AND checkout AND purchased AS f_paid
  FROM sessions
), cuts AS (
  SELECT 'source' AS dimension, utm_source AS segment, s.* FROM s
  UNION ALL SELECT 'platform', platform, s.* FROM s
  UNION ALL SELECT 'customer', CASE WHEN is_returning THEN 'returning' ELSE 'new' END, s.* FROM s
  UNION ALL SELECT 'category', category, s.* FROM s WHERE category IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT dimension, segment,
  count(*)::int                           AS sessions,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed)::int     AS viewed,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f_cart)::int     AS carted,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f_checkout)::int AS checkout,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE f_paid)::int     AS paid,
  round(sum(revenue))::float8             AS revenue
FROM cuts
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;
sql.mix_shift:
-- Sessions and orders by source, first four weeks vs last four weeks. Splits the
-- fall in blended conversion into "traffic mix changed" vs "conversion rates changed".
SELECT
  CASE WHEN day < DATE '2026-09-21' THEN 'first_4_weeks' ELSE 'last_4_weeks' END AS period,
  utm_source,
  count(*)::int                          AS sessions,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased)::int AS orders
FROM sessions
WHERE day < DATE '2026-09-21' OR day >= DATE '2026-10-26'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.release_impact:
-- Daily payment attempts and failures on iOS and Android around the iOS 4.2 release
-- (10 Oct 2026). Android is the control for a difference-in-differences read.
SELECT
  to_char((event_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS day,
  platform,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'payment_attempted')::int AS attempts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'payment_failed')::int    AS failures
FROM events
WHERE event_name IN ('payment_attempted', 'payment_failed')
  AND platform IN ('ios_app', 'android_app')
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.payment_errors:
-- Which error drives payment failures, by platform and app version.
SELECT platform, coalesce(app_version, 'web') AS app_version, error_code, count(*)::int AS failures
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'payment_failed'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY failures DESC;
sql.search_outcomes:
-- Sessions by search outcome, and how far each group gets.
SELECT
  CASE WHEN NOT searched THEN 'no search'
       WHEN zero_result_search THEN 'zero results'
       ELSE 'found results' END          AS search_outcome,
  count(*)::int                          AS sessions,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE viewed)::int    AS viewed,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased)::int AS orders
FROM sessions
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC;
sql.zero_result_queries:
-- The searches that return nothing, ranked by volume.
SELECT query, count(*)::int AS searches
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'search_performed' AND results_count = 0
GROUP BY query
ORDER BY searches DESC
LIMIT 10;
sql.cart_by_category:
-- Cart -> checkout -> order for carts with and without a mass gainer. The heavy-item
-- delivery fee is first shown in the cart, so mass gainer is the suspect.
WITH cart AS (
  SELECT session_id, bool_or(category = 'mass_gainer') AS has_mass_gainer
  FROM events WHERE event_name = 'add_to_cart'
  GROUP BY session_id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN c.has_mass_gainer THEN 'mass gainer in cart' ELSE 'other carts' END AS cart_type,
  count(*)::int                            AS carts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.checkout)::int  AS checkouts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.purchased)::int AS orders,
  round(sum(s.revenue) / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.purchased), 0))::float8 AS aov
FROM cart c JOIN sessions s USING (session_id)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
sql.coupon_friction:
-- Payment completion after checkout, by coupon outcome.
WITH c AS (
  SELECT session_id,
    bool_or(event_name = 'coupon_failed')  AS failed,
    bool_or(event_name = 'coupon_applied') AS applied,
    max(error_code) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'coupon_failed') AS error_code
  FROM events GROUP BY session_id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN c.failed THEN 'coupon failed' WHEN c.applied THEN 'coupon applied' ELSE 'no coupon' END AS coupon_outcome,
  count(*)::int                                                  AS checkouts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.purchased)::int                       AS orders,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.error_code = 'MIN_CART_VALUE')::int   AS min_cart_value_errors,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.error_code = 'COUPON_EXPIRED')::int   AS expired_errors
FROM sessions s JOIN c USING (session_id)
WHERE s.checkout
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC;
sql.cohort_retention:
-- Weekly acquisition cohorts: users with any session N weeks after their first week.
-- Only users first seen inside the window (users.first_seen), so earlier visitors
-- are not mistaken for new ones.
WITH first AS (
  SELECT user_id, date_trunc('week', first_seen)::date AS cohort FROM users
), activity AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.user_id, f.cohort,
    (date_trunc('week', s.day)::date - f.cohort) / 7 AS week_n
  FROM sessions s JOIN first f USING (user_id)
)
SELECT to_char(cohort, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS cohort, week_n::int AS week_n, count(*)::int AS users
FROM activity
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.experiments:
-- Per experiment and variant: exposed sessions and outcomes in the same session.
-- Exposure = the experiment_viewed event.
WITH exposed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT session_id, experiment, variant
  FROM events WHERE event_name = 'experiment_viewed'
)
SELECT e.experiment, e.variant,
  count(*)::int                             AS sessions,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.carted)::int     AS carted,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.checkout)::int   AS checkouts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.purchased)::int  AS orders,
  round(sum(s.revenue))::float8             AS revenue,
  round(stddev_samp(s.revenue) FILTER (WHERE s.purchased))::float8 AS order_value_sd
FROM exposed e JOIN sessions s USING (session_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.pdp_clickmap:
-- PDP clickmap and scrollmap: share of product-page sessions that clicked each element
-- or reached each scroll depth, plus the add-to-cart rate of those sessions.
WITH pdp AS (SELECT session_id, carted FROM sessions WHERE viewed)
SELECT 'click' AS kind, e.element AS item, bool_or(e.is_dead_click) AS dead,
  count(DISTINCT e.session_id)::int                          AS sessions,
  count(DISTINCT e.session_id) FILTER (WHERE p.carted)::int  AS carted
FROM events e JOIN pdp p USING (session_id)
WHERE e.event_name = 'element_clicked'
GROUP BY 2
UNION ALL
SELECT 'scroll', e.scroll_pct::text, false,
  count(DISTINCT e.session_id)::int,
  count(DISTINCT e.session_id) FILTER (WHERE p.carted)::int
FROM events e JOIN pdp p USING (session_id)
WHERE e.event_name = 'scroll_depth'
GROUP BY 2
ORDER BY 1, 4 DESC;
sql.reconciliation:
-- The funnel must agree with the raw event table, or nothing above can be trusted.
SELECT
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT session_id) FROM events)::int                                          AS raw_sessions,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM sessions)::int                                                          AS funnel_sessions,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE event_name = 'payment_completed')::int                      AS raw_orders,
  (SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE purchased) FROM sessions)::int                                 AS funnel_orders,
  (SELECT round(sum(revenue)) FROM events WHERE event_name = 'payment_completed')::float8        AS raw_revenue,
  (SELECT round(sum(revenue)) FROM sessions)::float8                                            AS funnel_revenue,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM sessions WHERE purchased AND NOT (viewed AND carted AND checkout))::int AS orders_skipping_steps,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events)::int                                             AS users,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM events)::int                                                            AS events;
sql.release_sessions:
-- Checkout -> paid conversion per platform, before the iOS 4.2 release and after
-- full adoption (16 Oct onward). Feeds the difference-in-differences estimate.
SELECT platform,
  CASE WHEN day < DATE '2026-10-10' THEN 'pre' ELSE 'post' END AS period,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE checkout)::int                AS checkouts,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE checkout AND purchased)::int  AS orders,
  round(sum(revenue))::float8                          AS revenue
FROM sessions
WHERE platform IN ('ios_app', 'android_app')
  AND (day < DATE '2026-10-10' OR day >= DATE '2026-10-16')
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.experiment_overlap:
-- Users exposed to both experiments: are the two assignments independent?
-- If bucketing were independent, each cell would hold about a quarter of users.
WITH a AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    max(variant) FILTER (WHERE experiment = 'pdp_sticky_atc')    AS sticky,
    max(variant) FILTER (WHERE experiment = 'one_page_checkout') AS one_page
  FROM events WHERE event_name = 'experiment_viewed'
  GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT sticky, one_page, count(*)::int AS users
FROM a WHERE sticky IS NOT NULL AND one_page IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.experiment_basket:
-- Mechanism check for the AOV guardrail: items per paid cart and share of paid
-- carts with more than one product, by variant.
WITH exposed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT session_id, experiment, variant FROM events WHERE event_name = 'experiment_viewed'
), items AS (
  SELECT session_id, count(DISTINCT product_id) AS products FROM events WHERE event_name = 'add_to_cart' GROUP BY session_id
)
SELECT e.experiment, e.variant,
  round(avg(i.products), 2)::float8                                      AS products_per_order,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE i.products > 1) / count(*), 1)::float8 AS multi_product_pct
FROM exposed e JOIN sessions s USING (session_id) JOIN items i USING (session_id)
WHERE s.purchased
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

-- Retention & lifecycle intelligence: every query behind /retention and /journeys.
-- Tables: customers, orders, order_items, products, campaign_sends (db/schema.sql).
-- Snapshot = end of 22 Nov 2026 IST. Same "-- @query <name>" convention as analysis.sql.
sql.crm_overview:
-- Headline retention numbers. 90-day repeat rate only counts customers who have had
-- 90 days to come back, so recent customers do not drag it down.
WITH snap AS (SELECT TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-23 00:00+05:30' AS t),
c AS (
  SELECT o.user_id, min(o.order_time) AS first_at, count(*) AS orders, sum(o.revenue) AS revenue,
         min(o.order_time) FILTER (WHERE o.order_number = 2) AS second_at
  FROM orders o GROUP BY o.user_id
)
SELECT
  count(*)::int                                                                      AS customers,
  sum(orders)::int                                                                   AS orders,
  round(sum(revenue))::float8                                                        AS revenue,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE orders >= 2) / count(*), 1)::float8           AS repeat_rate_pct,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE first_at <= (SELECT t FROM snap) - interval '90 days')::int AS customers_90d_tenure,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE first_at <= (SELECT t FROM snap) - interval '90 days' AND second_at <= first_at + interval '90 days')
        / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE first_at <= (SELECT t FROM snap) - interval '90 days'), 0), 1)::float8 AS repeat_90d_pct,
  round(sum(orders)::numeric / count(*), 2)::float8                                  AS orders_per_customer,
  (SELECT round(100.0 * sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1) / sum(revenue), 1) FROM orders)::float8 AS repeat_revenue_pct,
  (SELECT round(avg(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number = 1)) FROM orders)::float8   AS aov_first,
  (SELECT round(avg(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1)) FROM orders)::float8   AS aov_repeat
FROM c;
sql.repeat_trend:
-- Monthly orders split into first and repeat, to see whether growth is new-customer only.
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE order_number = 1)::int AS first_orders,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1)::int AS repeat_orders,
  round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number = 1))::float8 AS first_revenue,
  round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1))::float8 AS repeat_revenue
FROM orders
WHERE order_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-12-01 00:00+05:30'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
sql.time_to_second:
-- Days from first to second order, bucketed, for customers who placed a second order.
WITH g AS (
  SELECT o2.order_time::date - o1.order_time::date AS days
  FROM orders o1 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.user_id = o1.user_id AND o2.order_number = 2
  WHERE o1.order_number = 1
)
SELECT CASE WHEN days <= 15 THEN '0-15' WHEN days <= 30 THEN '16-30' WHEN days <= 45 THEN '31-45'
            WHEN days <= 60 THEN '46-60' WHEN days <= 90 THEN '61-90' ELSE '90+' END AS bucket,
       min(days)::int AS sort_key, count(*)::int AS customers
FROM g GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2;
sql.time_to_second_stats:
SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY o2.order_time::date - o1.order_time::date)::float8 AS median_days,
       percentile_cont(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY o2.order_time::date - o1.order_time::date)::float8 AS p25_days,
       percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY o2.order_time::date - o1.order_time::date)::float8 AS p75_days,
       count(*)::int AS customers
FROM orders o1 JOIN orders o2 ON o2.user_id = o1.user_id AND o2.order_number = 2
WHERE o1.order_number = 1;
sql.purchase_cohorts:
-- Monthly first-order cohorts: share of customers ordering again in month N after the first.
WITH c AS (
  SELECT user_id, date_trunc('month', min(order_time) AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS cohort FROM orders GROUP BY user_id
), a AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.user_id, c.cohort,
    (extract(year FROM age(date_trunc('month', o.order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'), c.cohort)) * 12
     + extract(month FROM age(date_trunc('month', o.order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'), c.cohort)))::int AS month_n
  FROM orders o JOIN c USING (user_id)
)
SELECT to_char(cohort, 'YYYY-MM') AS cohort, month_n, count(*)::int AS customers
FROM a WHERE cohort >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;
sql.replenishment:
-- Replenishment window per product: days between consecutive orders of the same product
-- by the same customer. The median is when a reminder should land.
WITH po AS (
  SELECT o.user_id, i.product_id, o.order_time::date AS d,
         lag(o.order_time::date) OVER (PARTITION BY o.user_id, i.product_id ORDER BY o.order_time) AS prev_d
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items i USING (order_id)
)
SELECT po.product_id, p.category, p.cycle_days,
  count(*)::int AS repurchases,
  percentile_cont(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY d - prev_d)::float8 AS p25,
  percentile_cont(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY d - prev_d)::float8 AS p50,
  percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY d - prev_d)::float8 AS p75
FROM po JOIN products p USING (product_id)
WHERE prev_d IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING count(*) >= 20
ORDER BY repurchases DESC;
sql.rfm:
-- RFM: recency, frequency, monetary scored 1-5 by quintile, then mapped to named segments.
WITH base AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    (DATE '2026-11-22' - max((order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date))::int AS recency_days,
    count(*)::int AS frequency,
    sum(revenue)::float8 AS monetary
  FROM orders GROUP BY user_id
), scored AS (
  SELECT *,
    6 - ntile(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS r,
    CASE WHEN frequency >= 4 THEN 5 WHEN frequency = 3 THEN 4 WHEN frequency = 2 THEN 3 ELSE 1 END AS f,
    ntile(5) OVER (ORDER BY monetary) AS m
  FROM base
), seg AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN r >= 4 AND f >= 4 THEN 'Champions'
      WHEN r >= 3 AND f >= 3 THEN 'Loyal'
      WHEN r <= 2 AND f >= 3 THEN 'At risk (repeat buyers)'
      WHEN r >= 4 AND f = 1 THEN 'New'
      WHEN r = 3 AND f = 1 THEN 'Needs a second order'
      WHEN r <= 2 AND f = 1 AND recency_days <= 180 THEN 'Hibernating'
      ELSE 'Lost'
    END AS segment
  FROM scored
)
SELECT segment, count(*)::int AS customers,
  round(avg(recency_days))::int AS avg_recency_days,
  round(avg(frequency), 2)::float8 AS avg_orders,
  round(avg(monetary))::float8 AS avg_revenue,
  round(sum(monetary))::float8 AS revenue
FROM seg GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
sql.churn_risk:
-- Churn risk: days since the last order against that product's replenishment cycle.
-- Overdue by 1.5x the cycle = at risk; 3x = lapsed.
WITH last AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (o.user_id) o.user_id, o.order_time, i.product_id
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items i USING (order_id)
  ORDER BY o.user_id, o.order_time DESC, i.price DESC
), cust AS (
  SELECT l.user_id, (DATE '2026-11-22' - (l.order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date)::float8 / p.cycle_days AS cycles_since,
         t.orders, t.revenue
  FROM last l JOIN products p USING (product_id)
  JOIN (SELECT user_id, count(*) AS orders, sum(revenue) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY 1) t USING (user_id)
)
SELECT CASE WHEN cycles_since < 1 THEN '1 · on track' WHEN cycles_since < 1.5 THEN '2 · due now'
            WHEN cycles_since < 3 THEN '3 · at risk' ELSE '4 · lapsed' END AS status,
  count(*)::int AS customers,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE orders >= 2)::int AS repeat_customers,
  round(sum(revenue))::float8 AS lifetime_revenue
FROM cust GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
sql.clv_by_source:
-- 180-day customer value by acquisition source, for customers with 180+ days of tenure.
WITH c AS (
  SELECT cu.user_id, cu.acquisition_source, cu.first_order_date FROM customers cu
  WHERE cu.first_order_date <= DATE '2026-11-22' - 180
)
SELECT c.acquisition_source,
  count(DISTINCT c.user_id)::int AS customers,
  round(sum(o.revenue)::numeric / count(DISTINCT c.user_id))::float8 AS revenue_180d,
  round(count(o.order_id)::numeric / count(DISTINCT c.user_id), 2)::float8 AS orders_180d
FROM c JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = c.user_id
  AND (o.order_time AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date < c.first_order_date + 180
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
sql.new_customers_by_source:
-- New customers acquired inside the 13-week event window, by acquisition source (for CAC).
SELECT acquisition_source, count(*)::int AS new_customers
FROM customers WHERE first_order_date >= DATE '2026-08-24'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
sql.campaign_results:
-- Lifecycle campaign readout. Conversion = any order within 14 days of the send (and 30
-- days, to check for pull-forward). Holdout rows were never messaged.
SELECT s.campaign, s.variant, s.channel,
  count(*)::int                                             AS recipients,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.delivered)::int                  AS delivered,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.read)::int                       AS read,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.clicked)::int                    AS clicked,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE o14.n > 0)::int                    AS converted_14d,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE o30.n > 0)::int                    AS converted_30d,
  round(coalesce(sum(o14.revenue), 0))::float8              AS revenue_14d,
  round(coalesce(sum(o14.discount), 0))::float8             AS discount_14d,
  round(coalesce(sum(o30.revenue), 0))::float8              AS revenue_30d,
  round(coalesce(sum(o30.discount), 0))::float8             AS discount_30d,
  coalesce(sum(o30.n), 0)::int                              AS orders_30d,
  round(stddev_samp(coalesce(o14.revenue, 0)))::float8      AS revenue_sd
FROM campaign_sends s
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(revenue) AS revenue, sum(discount) AS discount FROM orders o
  WHERE o.user_id = s.user_id AND o.order_time > s.send_time AND o.order_time <= s.send_time + interval '14 days'
) o14 ON true
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(revenue) AS revenue, sum(discount) AS discount FROM orders o
  WHERE o.user_id = s.user_id AND o.order_time > s.send_time AND o.order_time <= s.send_time + interval '30 days'
) o30 ON true
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY 1, 2 DESC;
sql.replenishment_by_orders:
-- Who the replenishment reminder actually moves: lift by how many orders the customer had.
SELECT CASE WHEN prior.n = 1 THEN '1 prior order' ELSE '2 prior orders' END AS customer_type, s.variant,
  count(*)::int AS recipients,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = s.user_id AND o.order_time > s.send_time
                                 AND o.order_time <= s.send_time + interval '14 days'))::int AS converted_14d
FROM campaign_sends s
JOIN LATERAL (SELECT count(*) AS n FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = s.user_id AND o.order_time < s.send_time) prior ON true
WHERE s.campaign = 'replenishment_reminder'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2 DESC;
sql.crm_reconciliation:
-- Orders in the event window must equal payment_completed events, order for order.
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE order_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-24 00:00+05:30')::int AS window_orders,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE event_name = 'payment_completed')::int                   AS payment_events,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM orders o JOIN events e ON e.order_id = o.order_id AND e.event_name = 'payment_completed'
     AND e.revenue = o.revenue)::int                                                          AS matched,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM customers)::int                                                       AS customers,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT user_id) FROM orders)::int                                           AS order_customers;
sql.run_rate:
-- Last 28 days (26 Oct - 22 Nov): the baseline for the growth model.
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM sessions WHERE day >= DATE '2026-10-26')::int                      AS sessions,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE order_number = 1)::int                                             AS first_orders,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1)::int                                             AS repeat_orders,
  round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number = 1))::float8                               AS first_revenue,
  round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE order_number > 1))::float8                               AS repeat_revenue,
  round(sum(discount))::float8                                                              AS discounts
FROM orders WHERE order_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-26 00:00+05:30';
